primary_claim: R-lens (J-lens with Layer-wise Relevance Propagation rules substituted into the backward pass) produces substantially more faithful and causally important early-layer readouts than J-lens, with the quantitative pass@10 advantage over J-lens growing with model scale (largest for the 284B-parameter DeepSeek-V4-Flash MoE), and ablating R-lens-identified directions causes larger accuracy drops than ablating J-lens or logit-lens directions on nearly all tested models.

effect.metric: pass@10 (intermediate concept in top-10 lens readout), averaged over layers/categories
effect.value: R-lens advantage over J-lens increases with model scale, largest for DeepSeek-V4-Flash (284B/13B-active MoE); no advantage for the smallest dense and MoE models tested

contradicts_or_qualifies: Suggests J-lens's noisy early-layer readouts do not necessarily reflect an absence of linearly-accessible, causally-relevant content at those layers, since R-lens recovers coherent, causally important readouts at the same early layers
limitations_stated: No R-lens advantage observed for the smallest dense and MoE models tested

R-lens is mainly a tool for more faithfully tracking computation over layers rather than detecting concept presence, since most early-surfaced concepts also appear later and would eventually be read by J-lens anyway
The probe-derived 'earliest layer' upper bound used for comparison is a crude benchmark not to be taken too seriously
quote: R-lens shows a substantial quantitative advantage over J-lens that increases as models scale, measured across a variety of evaluation categories.
